title: C#: Exporting the project before building changes can lose scene data from external change
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible:
- v4.4.1.stable.mono.official [49a5bc7b6]
- v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]
- v4.6.dev4.mono.official [bd2ca13c6] (Required `Include Script Contents` on due to #112918)


### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.5599) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 threads) - 15.76 GiB memory

### Issue description

On the project I'm working on, I pushed a change that added a signal to a script and connected the signal in a scene via editor. Someone else pulled the change, but exported the project before building for the editor. The other person's export had bugs due to the signal connection no longer existing in the exported version, but was bug free when running in editor. 
While this issue can be avoided by remembering to build before exporting, the greater issue was that later exports still lost the signal connection. Fixing exports required deleting the `.godot` folder or modifying the afflicted scene. So it would be nice if missing the build button didn't cause a more involved cleanup.

### Steps to reproduce

The MRP is set up with a simple script with a signal called on ready. The signal is hooked up to make a white color rect visible, so if the signal is missing, the screen should be the default gray.

1. Open the MRP and build the project
2. Comment out lines 6 and 10 in `ScriptWithSignal`
3. Build the project again
4. Uncomment lines 6 and 10 in `ScriptWithSignal`. At this point, the project is in the same state as having uncompiled changes like when pulling from source control.
5. Export the project
6. Run the executable (screen should be fully white if signal exported correctly)

Notes:
- Do not open and save changes to `SceneWithSignal`. The signal has to exist in the file to properly recreate the issue.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[SignalLostOnExport.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23812040/SignalLostOnExport.zip)
